## Opponent Reads

**Player 2**: **LAG/maniac, extreme calling station postflop.** 3-bets extremely wide (mid pairs, trash). Calls down with virtually anything. **As PFA**: c-bets flop then checks/folds turn when called — profitable float spot. Also sometimes check-folds flop entirely on dry low boards without c-betting. Checks flop then bets turn = delayed value (real hand). **As caller**: Check-calls flop, DONK-LEADS turn with real hands/draws, then checks river and calls all-ins with top pair weak kicker. When aggressor shows weakness (checks river after betting earlier streets), P2 fires big river bets — opportunistic. **Exploit**: 3-bet for value. Value bet EXTREMELY thin. Do NOT bluff. Float flop c-bets. Turn donk-leads (as non-PFA) = real hands. Don't show weakness vs P2 — they'll pounce.

**Player 3**: **Selectively aggressive, skilled.** Opens and 4-bets wider than premium (suited aces as semi-bluffs). 3-bets from SB vs late-position steals. **Confirmed trapper** — check-calls multiple streets with two pair+. River checks can be traps. Folds dry boards without connections. **Exploit**: C-bet dry boards. Turn leads after flop checks = completed draw. Don't value-bet thin on river. Can call wider vs 4-bets. Tighten steals when P3 in blinds.

**Player 4**: **Wide VPIP (~50%), passive preflop but calls 3-bets with suited junk.** Do NOT 3-bet as a bluff expecting folds. 3-bet for VALUE/isolation — P4 will call with dominated holdings. Limp-reraise = strong (99+). Shoves AA preflop. **Postflop**: EXTREMELY sticky — calls river with top pair bad kicker, bottom pair, even 9-high. **When opponent checks (shows weakness), P4 fires** — exploitable by check-calling or check-raising for value. River shoves do NOT always = strength — confirmed shoved with bottom pair. **Exploit**: 3-bet for VALUE only. Value bet EXTREMELY wide postflop — #1 value target. NEVER bluff postflop. Can check strong hands to induce P4 bets. Respect check-raises, donk-bets, limp-reraises. Call river shoves lighter than default.

**Player 5**: **Nit (~8-10% VPIP).** Any preflop raise = strong. Limps with hands they're willing to defend — CALLS raises over limps (does NOT always fold to isolation raises). **Four postflop lines**: (1) Single donk-bet then folds to raises/turn barrels — two-barrel bluff. (2) Donk-bet + shove = strong draw. (3) Multi-street barreling = nutted (FOLD without nuts). (4) Passive calling = weak, can triple-barrel. **Exploit**: Two-barrel bluff line 1. FOLD to multi-street aggression. Triple-barrel passive mode. Don't expect limps to fold to raises.

**Player 6**: **Tight-ish raiser (~19% PFR).** 3-bets = QQ+/AK. Cold 4-bets = AA/KK. C-bets flop then folds to turn donk-leads. Bets flop+turn but check-folds river when he misses or faces aggression. **KEY WEAKNESS**: Folds QQ/KK on ace-high boards. Folds to sustained double-barrels. **Exploit**: Fold to 3-bets/4-bets. Isolate limps freely. Bluff ace-high/scary boards. Double-barrel. If P6 checks after betting two streets, fire big.

**Player 7**: **Wider than TAG — calls broadways, wide from blinds.** Passive preflop, AGGRESSIVE postflop — donk-leads and double-barrels with strength. Raises flop with just top pair on paired boards (spewy). Once committed, calls down with one pair. **Exploit**: Value bet relentlessly when ahead. Don't bluff once they've shown aggression.

## My Table Image & Approach

**Image**: Ultra-tight. Only showdown: AQ (top pair top kicker). Image is highly credible — bluffs/steals should get maximum respect. Leverage this early in next session before it erodes.

**Session 1 validation**: Patience + selective aggression + value betting stations = +$880 (+88% ROI). Strategy is confirmed profitable. Resist the urge to widen — card dead stretches are fine as long as big pots are won when entering.

**Confirmed leaks to avoid**:
1. **Offsuit broadways (KJo, KQo)**: Play poorly postflop. FOLD facing raises; only open late position.
2. **Weak aces (A2-AT offsuit)**: FOLD unless stealing or suited.
3. **Mid pairs**: Fold without set-mining conditions.

## Core Strategy

1. **VPIP target: 20-25%.** Tight discipline is an edge at this table.
2. **Hand selection**: Premiums (TT+, AJ+, KQs) for value. Suited connectors/small pairs ONLY in position vs limpers. ATs+ from steal positions.
3. **Station exploit (P2, P4, P7)**: Value bet wide, NEVER bluff, isolate limps. 3-bet P4's opens for VALUE (they call wide with junk). Don't show weakness vs P2.
4. **P5 (nit)**: Two-barrel bluff single donk-bets. FOLD to multi-street aggression. Don't iso-raise light expecting folds.
5. **P6 (exploitable)**: Bluff ace-high/scary boards. Double-barrel. Fire river if P6 checks after betting two streets. Fold to preflop aggression.
6. **P3 (skilled)**: Tighten steals. Don't thin value-bet rivers (traps). Most dangerous opponent.
7. **Threat hierarchy**: P3 (skilled) > P2 (LAG volume) > P7 (spewy) > P4 (station) > P6 (exploitable) > P5 (nit).

**Opponent Profiles:**

UTG opens premium (QQ+/AK/AQ), 3-bets only premium over EP opens, 4-b aggression with marginal holdings — confirms profitable thin value betting. Shows delayed aggression (check-turn/bet-river) with value-heavy ranges. Respects early position strength — avoid light defends against their 3-bets.
- Player 2: Passive-aggressive station — high fold-to-3-bet tendency, weak donk-leads, calls down with marginal made hands. Confirmed pattern exploitable by flop bets. Folds to turn pressure after c-betting — profitable to float and raise turn. Wide flatting range from BB and late position — value bet thinly on later streets.
- Player 3: Nit — EP opens TT+/AQG with weak holdings. High c-bet frequency on low boards but shows weakness by checking turn after betting flop — profitable to float and apply turn/river pressure. Flat-calls EP raises with speculative hands (suited connectors, small pairs). River bets after checking through strong boards are value-heavy (trips+) — avoid bluff-catching without strong reads.
- Player 4: LAG — wide EP opening range (includes suited connectors/weak aces), aggressive c-betting, but folds to turn pressure without strong holdings. Flat-calls late position raises passively — exploitable by postflop aggression in position. Shows multi-way passivity on coordinated boards — bet when checked to. Calls down with weak pairs in 3-bet pots — value bet wider on later streets when committed.
- Player 6: LAG — frequent late position opens, folds to 3-bet pressure. Triple barrels dry boards but gives up on river after turn calls — profitable to bluff river when checked to. Shows aggression on paired boards — likely value-heavy when betting multiple streets. Respects early position raises — abandons speculative hands facing strong ranges.
- Player 7: Tight-passive — premium-only 3-bets, extreme postflop passivity. Checks/folds multiple streets without initiative — highly exploitable by betting any equity. Limps weak hands late position, folds to flop c-bets after flatting preflop.

- Profit came from selectively aggressive plays in favorable spots — confirms value of patience combined with well-timed aggression.

**Strategic Learnings:**  
- Primary targets: Player 2 (flop bets when they check after preflop strength, turn pressure after c-bets), Player 3 (float flop → bet turn/river when they check), Player 4 (3-bet bluff their EP opens, apply postflop pressure in position), Player 7 (bet any street when they show passivity).
- Avoid light defends against Player 1’s 3-bets and Player 6’s early position raises.
- Multi-street bluffs with position highly effective against opponents showing sequential weakness.

**Opponent Profiles & Tendencies:**

Capable of massive multi-street bluffs with pure air and delayed stabs when checked to. Very sticky post-flop (floats with just A-high). *Exploit:* Widen bluff-catching and value-betting ranges. 3-bet aggressively for value preflop. Beware of traps when they flat flop raises and lead turns with nutted hands.
- **Player 2 (Extreme LAG / Calling Station):** Wide preflop range (e.g., J9o, weak suited Qx), 3-bets light from blinds/BTN. Capable of folding to preflop 3-bets after opening, but post-flop is an absolute station (floats with J-high, calls massive river overbet shoves with marginal top pairs). *Exploit:* NEVER bluff post-flop. Value bet relentlessly, including massive overbets/shoves on scary runouts for pure value. *Exception:* Folds to small c-bets on dry boards when defending BB in single-raised pots.
- **Player 4 (Aggressive / Spewy Station):** High VPIP, limps garbage but also limp-reraises. 3-bets wide but folds to 4-bets (balances by 5-bet jamming premiums like AA). Post-flop station (calls turns with gutshots/weak flush draws, rivers with 9-high air). Capable of massive overbet river bluffs when their draws miss. *Exploit:* NEVER bluff post-flop. Value bet relentlessly. Isolate their limps. 4-bet their 3-bets (value and bluff), but ALWAYS fold to their 5-bet jams. Bluff-catch massive river bombs if obvious draws miss and you hold top pair+.
- **Player 5 (Passive / Recreational):** Classic limp/caller preflop; typically only open-raises or 3-bets with premium hands. *Exploit:* Value bet thinly, fold to their aggression.
- **Player 6 (Loose-Passive):** Limp/calls preflop and plays fit-or-fold post-flop (check-folds easily when missing). *Exploit:* Isolate their limps preflop; c-bet frequently as bluffs since they will fold their missed hands.

**My Table Image & Adjustments:**
- **Ultra-Nit Image Solidified:** I just played an extremely tight session (folding 19 out of 20 hands). The table views me as an absolute rock who only plays premiums. 
- **Next Session Exploit:** I must capitalize on this ultra-tight image. I should drastically widen my steal range from late position, 3-bet light preflop, and aggressively c-bet/semi-bluff post-flop, as opponents will give my aggression maximum respect. 
- **Counter-Exploit:** Because my image is so tight, if any opponent (especially passive ones like P5 or P6) plays back at me or raises my bets, I must fold all marginal holdings immediately—they will only do this with nutted hands.

**Opponent Profiles (Session-Refined & Confirmed)**

- **Player 1 – Loose-Leaning TAG (Aggressive Pre, River Value-Heavy):**  
  Mixes preflop approaches and 3-bets strong broadways, not just premiums.  
  Postflop lines often structured and value-driven; big river bets remain heavily value-weighted.  
  → Do not over-bluff rivers.  
  → Bluff-catch cautiously vs large river bets.

- **Player 3 – Passive Value-Trapper (Delayed River Stabs):**  
  Tight EP opens. Prefers call-down lines with strong but non-nut hands. Rarely bluff-raises.  
  Raises on later streets are strongly value-weighted.  
  → 3-bet EP opens for fold equity.

  Wide opens, light 3-bets, attacks capped ranges. Capable of polar river aggression.  
  Will call down lighter than population, especially in 3-bet pots.

  Conservative preflop; aggression skews value-heavy.

  → Overfold to strong multi-street lines.

- **Player 6 – Tight, Value-Heavy, Honest Postflop:**  
  Strength-weighted preflop opens. Generally straightforward postflop.

  → Apply pressure on scare-card rivers.  
  → Respect early aggression.

  Very strength-heavy across all streets.  
  → Steal relentlessly.

OPPONENT READS:
- Player 1: Spewy LAG. Opens extremely wide, 3-bets light in position, calls 3-bets light (A8o-type hands), and floats flops with high-card hands. Barrels turns aggressively but will check turns on scare cards (A-high, completing draws) **AND with marginal made hands for pot control/inducement**. Bets rivers aggressively when checked to on safe runouts (paired boards, blanks), representing strength. **When Player 1 just calls preflop (no raise), plays more passively postflop - checks multiple streets and folds to turn aggression.** Exploit by 3-betting wide for value, applying pressure when they show passivity, and never bluffing rivers after they check.

- Player 2: EXTREME LAG when opening, but becomes straightforward and sticky when calling raises. As PFR, frequently c-bets but **will check-fold dry flops when missing, not just turns**. More likely to give up on turn when called and facing aggression. Calls down with marginal made hands that have potential, reluctant to fold once invested. Donk-bets flops in raised AND 3-bet pots but folds to any raise. In limped pots, shows multi-street aggression even without preflop initiative (delayed c-bets, turn+river barrels). **As preflop caller in raised pots, capable of river aggression when original aggressor shows weakness, particularly against opponents known to check-fold rivers.** Exploit by raising their donk bets liberally, floating their c-bets and betting turns when they check, and exercising caution in limped pots when they fire multiple streets. Value bet thinner against them when you have a real hand.

- Player 3: Station tendencies are INITIATIVE-DEPENDENT. **When CALLING in single-raised pots: extreme station, slow-plays monsters (two pair+), check-calls multiple streets with strong hands.** When RAISING in single-raised pots: more capable of folding to later aggression, particularly on scary runouts or against aggressive opponents. Aggressive in 3-bet pots (4-bets suited Aces/broadways). Opens wide and defends 3-bets frequently. In limped pots, plays draws passively but bets made hands aggressively.

- Player 4: **RECLASSIFIED: LAG/loose caller, not Elite TAG.** Raises preflop with extremely wide range including weak suited hands (Q6s) and calls 3-bets with same weak range. In 3-bet pots as the CALLER, plays fit-or-fold loosely - calls flops with weak pairs, bets turns when checked to (can be bluff or marginal value), and makes very thin river calls. **When they show aggression multi-way, range remains strong - fold marginal hands.** Heads-up, capable of big river calls with weak pairs, not just bluffs when draws miss. Exploit by 3-betting them relentlessly for value with any decent hand, applying flop pressure on coordinated boards when they call 3-bets, and value betting rivers thinly against their calling tendencies. Do not attempt to bluff them in single-raised or 3-bet pots - they call too light.

- Player 5: LAG with both preflop and postflop aggression. 3-bets with strong, polarized range (not just a caller). **When they just call preflop, postflop aggression is VARIED: includes donk-bets (often large sizing), turn barrels, AND delayed river aggression after passive earlier streets.** Shows call-down tendencies but can fold to river pressure. When they 3-bet preflop, they show continued aggression on later streets. Exploit by respecting their 3-bets, but attacking their postflop aggression when they flat preflop. Their multi-street commitment is real strength, not bluff-heavy, but they can be pushed off marginal holdings on the river.

- Player 6: Tight 3-bettor (QQ+, AK) but opens wider than premium hands in single-raised pots (A9o-type hands). Capable of triple-barreling with marginal pairs in single-raised pots when they have initiative. Also capable of turn aggression as caller when checked to after calling preflop and flop. As caller in 3-bet pots, leads flops but folds to turn pressure when facing aggression. Straightforward postflop - folds when board misses their range. Exploit by folding to their 3-bets without premium holdings, applying pressure on unfavorable boards, but respect their multi-street aggression in single-raised pots regardless of initiative and target them in 3-bet pots when they are the caller.

STRATEGIC NOTES:
- Critical vulnerability identified: Overplaying KQ-type hands in marginal spots. Two significant losses (-$310, -$90) suggest these hands are often dominated or facing stronger ranges. Adjust by folding KQ to early position opens and 3-bets, especially against Players 1, 4, and 6.
- Floating LAG c-bets and attacking turn checks is profitable, especially against Players 2 and 5 when they are PFR in single-raised pots.
- 3-bet pot dynamics are opponent-specific and position-dependent: value bet thinner against stations (Player 1, 3 when calling, **Player 4 in all situations**), but respect aggression from tight players (Player 6) AND from LAGs who 3-bet preflop (Player 5). Target Player 6 specifically when they are caller (not aggressor) in 3-bet pots.
- When facing flop leads in 3-bet pots from TAG players, especially multi-way, treat as extreme strength.
- Player 5's 3-bet range is strong and continues postflop. When they flat preflop, their postflop aggression is more exploitable but includes delayed moves.
- Scare cards on turn (A-high, completing draws) can slow LAGs down, but they often fire rivers on safe runouts. Don't assume shutdown after turn check.
- Even elite TAGs (Player 4) can make big river bluffs heads-up when draws miss and opponent shows weakness.
- **Respect river aggression from LAGs who have shown earlier passivity (e.g., Player 5's delayed river bets). When they fire after checking earlier streets, their range is weighted toward value and credible bluffs that exploit station tendencies.**
- **Major reclassification alert: When opponent's revealed range contradicts profile, trust the evidence. Player 4's Q6s in a 3-bet pot reveals they are not TAG - adjust exploitation accordingly.**

SELF-IMAGE & ADJUSTMENTS:
- Table image: Extremely tight (folded 70% of hands). This is profitable but creates exploitation opportunity. Plan: Begin mixing in selective 3-bet bluffs and river raises against thinking opponents who respect my tight image, particularly targeting Players 1 and 2.
- Continue selective hand selection but increase aggression factor when entering pots to balance image.
- Primary leak to address: Stop bleeding chips with marginal broadway hands (KQ, KJ, QJ) in raised pots without clear initiative. These hands perform poorly against the calling/3-betting ranges of Players 1, 3, and 4.

- **Player 2** is a **foldy LAG** (VPIP ~57%, PFR ~43%) who opens extremely wide from late positions, including bluffs, weak A-x, and suited connectors. However, **when they call both a flop c-bet and a turn barrel out of position—especially on dry, disconnected boards—their range is heavily weighted toward made hands (pairs 66–99, weak top pair)** and **bluffs are exceptionally rare**. **Exploit**: **Bluff the turn aggressively only when the turn card improves your perceived range or you hold blockers to their likely holdings (e.g., A-x on A-high boards)**. **Avoid pure air bluffs on brick turns after flop calls**. **Do not expect river folds after they call two streets**.

- **Player 4** is a confirmed **passive, wide-raising calling station**: opens or limps wide from early position (including weak pairs, broadways, suited connectors) and **rarely folds postflop**, even to large turn or river bets. **Exploit**: **Never bluff them postflop**. **Value bet thinly but avoid overbetting**. **Preflop, 3-bet only for value—bluff 3-bets are wasted**. **Calling their opens out of position with marginal hands is a consistent leak**.

- **Player 5** is **tight-passive with low showdown tolerance**: folds to aggression unless holding top/middle pair or better. **Exploit**: **Apply consistent turn pressure with overpairs, top pair, or strong draws when they call the flop**. They are **not a bluff-catcher** and **fold too often to double barrels**.

- **Player 7** remains a **weak-tight recreational**: limps weak broadways, checks down air, never bluffs. **Exploit**: **Bet for thin value and avoid bluffing**. **They overfold to aggression but under-defend marginal holdings**.

- **Player 3** is a **loose TAG who calls down lighter than average** with marginal pairs and weak top pairs. **Not easily bluffed**, but **can be outplayed by strong, consistent value lines**. **Avoid light 3-bets unless you have blockers or strong equity**.

- **Your table image** is **tight-aggressive**, which continues to generate strong early-street fold equity—especially against Player 2. However, **this session confirmed that bluffing multi-street with zero equity on static boards is unprofitable against opponents who demonstrate willingness to call multiple streets with medium-strength hands**. **Adjustment**: **Reserve turn barrels for hands with at least some equity (backdoor draws, overcards with blockers) or when the turn card favors your perceived range**.

- **Strategic refinements**:  
  - **Preflop discipline is the highest-leverage area**: **Tighter calling ranges out of position and more selective 3-betting (especially against foldy LAGs like Player 2) will improve win rate**.  
  - **Postflop on dry boards**: **Hands with only bottom/middle pair and no backdoor equity are bluff-catchers at best against passive or calling-station opponents—default to folding unless facing a known frequent bluffer**.  
  - **Position remains critical**: **Marginal hands played OOP led to consistent small losses; reserve wider calls for in-position spots where you can control pot size and extract value**.  
  - **Fold equity decays rapidly after opponents call multiple streets**, especially on static boards—**adjust bluffing frequency accordingly**.

- **Final opponent classifications (stable across sessions)**:  
  - **Player 2**: Foldy LAG  
  - **Player 3**: Loose TAG (light caller)  
  - **Player 4**: Passive calling station  
  - **Player 5**: Tight-passive (folds to pressure)  
  - **Player 7**: Weak-tight recreational  

- **Key takeaway**: **Tightening preflop ranges out of position and refining bluff criteria on later streets—based on board texture, opponent tendencies, and your own range composition—will yield the largest improvements in future sessions**.
